exact_admitted_claim: Within the tested five-node equal-shortest-route specimen, permuting competing first-hop edge_id labels while preserving the tested directed endpoint relation can change the selected coordinate path. Equivalently: EDGE_ID LABELING IS BEHAVIORALLY MATERIAL TO ROUTE SELECTION WITHIN THE TESTED APPARATUS.
exact_claim_ceiling: This admission establishes only bounded behavioral materiality of edge_id labeling under the realized specimen and frozen apparatus. It does not establish that edge IDs are inherently semantic, that routing should be permutation-invariant, that Atlas is globally defective, that the behavior generalizes beyond the tested equal-shortest-route geometry, or that any replacement tie-break/routing policy is preferable.
unresolved_consequence: Any downstream use that requires the selected coordinate path to remain invariant under otherwise topology-preserving edge_id relabeling now has an unresolved dependency: whether that representation sensitivity is acceptable intended behavior or a property requiring a separately designed pressure and policy decision.
surviving_relation: edge-id permutation can alter selected equal-hop coordinate path in the tested producer
